newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand raises 96/97 coffee export forecast.
newsitem.headline: Thailand raises 96/97 coffee export forecast.

text.p: Thailand will increase its estimate for 1996/97 (October-November) coffee exports to around 53,000 tonnes from a previous projection of 32,000 tonnes, a commerce ministry official said on Monday.
The increase would be due to better-than-expected coffee production, now expected to hit 83,000 tonnes, he told Reuters.
"Earlier, coffee planters forecast that the output this year would drop to 62,000 tonnes due to rains," the official said.
"But the agriculture ministry insisted that the output would be above 80,000 tonnes. And it seems that the ministry is right," he said.
Thailand exported 60,000 tonnes of coffee in the 1995/96 season.
The government sees 1996/97 domestic demand at 30,000 tonnes and will buy the rest from planters at a guaranteed price of 30 baht a kg ($1.20) for exports.
